scope: Phase 4 independent one-hop and reviewed-note experiments; defaults remain lexical-only until host evidence justifies otherwise

graph.selection: Ordinary discovery prefers outgoing resolved-local imports; usage intent prefers incoming importers. Rank incoming by non-anchor query relevance and explicit path evidence before filename ties. For high-degree seeds suppress unmatched incoming files unless usage intent is explicit.
graph.packing: Interleave up to two neighbor candidates after the first three lexical candidates, then remaining lexical candidates; keep the total 200-candidate pool and existing response/item/per-file limits. Graph presence does not prove execution or callers.

notes.selection: Only valid accepted notes. Match specific scopes to ranked evidence, or require a positive title/rationale/body query match and scope intersecting eligible files. Generic all-repository scopes require a text match. Parse YAML 1.2 as data with no aliases/custom tags. Duplicate IDs are invalid.
notes.packing: Notes are atomic source excerpts, never silently shortened. Reserve bounded references for preselected omitted notes and count all warnings/metadata. Expansion requires notes opt-in and revalidates current review status, source bytes and binding freshness.
notes.research_authoring: Evaluation-only researcher notes summarize pre-fix README content using fixed repository-level recipes, never future diffs or task-specific answers. Reviewer identity is the implementation agent, not an upstream maintainer/human endorsement.

evaluation: Use the original fixed 20 diagnostic development cases, with no holdout/model calls. Before adding notes, lexical-only v2 must reproduce saved controls. All L/G/N/GN conditions then share the same pre-fix source plus evaluation-note files, use exact full-envelope accounting, and are evaluated at 1000/2000/4000 tokens. Record added/displaced labeled evidence and note/neighbor delivery. Offline source-overlap metrics do not measure decision-note utility; future agent trials are required.
